body:
Upgrades the single resolved proxy-addr dependency from 2.0.7 to 2.0.8 and adds four regression/control tests for CVE-2026-90711 / GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h. Only package.json, package-lock.json and test/proxy-addr-security.test.js change.

| QA check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing application tests before change | 49 passed |
| New regression against 2.0.7 | 2 assertion failures; 2 controls passed |
| Regression after upgrade | 4 passed |
| Existing + new tests after change | 53 passed, 0 failed |
| Lint | Passed |
| Hosted CI on exact PR head | Passed |
| Comparable OSV rescan | Selected finding removed; zero new findings |

Existing HTTP integration tests cover dashboard rendering, liveness/readiness, upstream failures and recovery. No tests were disabled. Node 20.20.2 / npm 10.9.9; the repository has no build script.

[QA execution and evidence](https://axiom-stage.truxt.ai/b560f8c8/backend/issues/AXM-707) · [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/truxt-ai/ops-dashboard/actions/runs/40281260398/job/121434854922) · [Complete original scan](https://axiom-stage.truxt.ai/b560f8c8/backend/issues/AXM-698)

Exact head: `2b6a64fb5edc323081162457b989878a36c686ff`. OSV Scanner 2.6.0 scanned the baseline at 06:37:50–06:37:53 UTC and this head at 06:39:42–06:39:44 UTC on 2026-10-26, using the same configuration, full lockfile inventory, no ignores and the live OSV API. Both inventoried 175 package versions. Canonical findings decreased from 50 to 49; exactly the selected proxy-addr advisory was removed. **49 findings remain: 1 critical, 22 high, 22 medium, 4 low.** This is not a clean-repository claim.

The regression proves dependency behavior under the advisory's trust-subnet precondition. This application's Express trust-proxy setting remains disabled; current application exploitability is not established.

Native Axiom execution recorded 108,393 fresh input tokens, 10,347 output tokens, 2,219,264 cached input tokens and $3.82 cost. Temporary runtime proof files were cleaned at completion; test outputs have been recovered from the retained native command transcript, and both recovered raw scan files match their original recorded SHA-256 hashes. Recovery provenance is documented with the retained evidence. Final raw scan SHA-256: `6141f6e407803104fd4926b47d05ec38d68367d7b823cb3caded452245e723b7`.

Leave open for review. No merge or deployment has been performed.
